content.question: In the Episode 1 demo the instructor replaced a color name used across multiple XML locations — which editor trick did he use to change every occurrence at once?

options.text: Select the text and use Replace All (Cmd/Ctrl+F then Replace All)
Manually edit each XML file one-by-one
Run a Gradle task to recompile resources

content.explanation: He selected the color name, opened the find/replace and used Replace All to update every occurrence across the screen.
hints: Use Replace All to change every occurrence

content.question: When the instructor wanted to change a button's sharp corners to rounded ones, which drawable file type did he create to hold that shape?
content.explanation: He created a new drawable resource file (a shape XML) to define solid color, corners (radius) and stroke for the button background.
hints: Use drawable resource file for component backgrounds
Vector and image assets are not used for shape drawables

content.question: Inside a shape drawable the instructor used an element to set the fill color — which XML tag is used to provide a uniform fill?
content.explanation: The <solid> tag is used inside a shape drawable to set a uniform fill color (e.g., the vivid blue used by the instructor).
hints: solid provides a flat color fill

content.question: To round all four corners of the rectangle shape the instructor set a single attribute — which attribute controls the corner radius applied to every corner?
content.explanation: Using the 'radius' attribute in the <corners> element applies the same radius to all four corners of the shape.

content.question: The instructor added an outline around the shape using a tag that accepts a color and width — which tag is this?
content.explanation: The <stroke> element defines an outline for a shape and accepts a color and width attribute (the instructor used a small width like 1dp).
hints: stroke sets outline color and width
Use small widths for subtle outlines

content.question: After applying the drawable background the instructor clicked the button in the emulator but nothing happened — what was the missing step he pointed out?

options.text: No functionality was wired in the Kotlin/Java controller (no click handler)
The drawable was not referenced in XML
The button was disabled by default

content.explanation: The UI looked correct but lacked controller code — the instructor emphasized that XML alone doesn't provide functionality; you must add handlers in Kotlin/Java.
hints: Controller files (Kotlin/Java) add behavior like click listeners

content.question: Which root element did the instructor replace with 'shape' when creating the drawable for the button?
content.explanation: He replaced the 'selector' root with 'shape' because he wanted a shape drawable, not a state selector.
hints: selector is used for state-based drawables

content.question: What is the default shape type for a shape drawable if none is specified?
content.explanation: The default shape for a shape drawable is 'rectangle'.
hints: You can change it to 'oval' or other types

content.question: If you want to round only the top-right corner of a drawable, which attributes would you use?
content.explanation: Use the corner-specific attributes (topRightRadius, topLeftRadius, etc.) within <corners> to set individual corner radii.
hints: Use individual corner attributes for per-corner control

content.question: Which tag inside a shape drawable sets an outline color and width?
content.explanation: The <stroke> element defines the outline color and width for the shape drawable.

content.question: Where should you place a drawable resource file for a button background in an Android project?
content.explanation: Drawable XML files belong in the res/drawable/ directory.

content.question: How do you apply a drawable named 'button_design' as the background of a view in XML?
content.explanation: Use android:background='@drawable/button_design' to set a drawable resource as a view background.

content.question: When using the Tricolours website the instructor copied a hex color code — how is that typically done on the site?

options.text: Click the color swatch to copy the hex code

content.explanation: He clicked the color to copy its hex code from the Tricolours website.
hints: Sites often show 'copy' on color swatches

content.question: If the transcript shows '30 dB' when setting corner radius, what is the correct Android unit intended?
content.explanation: The transcript typo 'dB' was intended to be the Android density-independent pixel 'dp'.

content.question: What stroke width did the instructor recommend for a subtle outline on the drawable?
content.explanation: He suggested using a small stroke width like 1dp to keep the outline subtle and visually pleasing.
hints: 1dp is commonly used for fine outlines
